title: How Does Going Public Affect Employee Satisfaction? Evidence from Glassdoor Reviews
eligible_reason: Generalized DiD on review-level Glassdoor data assigned to firms: post_ipo_dummy is a 0/1 indicator that switches on for reviews posted after the firm's own IPO event date (S-1 filing date, or first trading date when the S-1 date is missing) and stays on; IPO dates are firm-specific and spread over 2008-2022 (59 distinct adoption quarters among switchers in the synthetic data); private firms that never IPO form a large never-treated group; the baseline regression uses firm and year-quarter fixed effects with no controls. The baseline column (firm + year_qtr FE, no controls), the baseline dynamic specification (relative-year bins, firm + year_qtr FE, no controls) and the firm-month window regressions (firm + year_qtr FE, no controls) qualify. Columns adding reviewer characteristics (female_employee, regular_employee, college_graduate) or extra additive FE (state_code, job_title_code, tenure_years) do not.
design_notes: Review-level repeated cross-section (3.94 million reviews in the synthetic file), May 2008 to Dec 2022, 60 year-quarters, 192,912 firms (synthetic). Outcome overall_rating_std = standardized Glassdoor overall rating. Treatment post_ipo_dummy as above; years_since_ipo and months_since_ipo measure relative time. Never-treated: private_company == 1 (78% of reviews). Always-treated: firms that went public before 2008 (public_company == 1 with post_ipo_dummy == 1 throughout; 2,196 firms, 14.7% of reviews in the synthetic file). Switchers: 783 firms (5.8% of reviews) with first treated quarters ranging 2008Q1-2022Q4. Clustering variable cluster_var is not documented in the README; in the synthetic data it coincides exactly with firm-by-review-year cells (664,419 groups). Controls female_employee regular_employee college_graduate are reviewer-level characteristics that vary across observations within firm-quarter, so they are time-varying controls under the protocol. The dynamic specification (Table 5) uses bins minus3 (< -2 years), minus2, minus1, one, two, three (> 2 years), with the IPO year (zero) omitted together with never-treated reviews. Other tables use interactions with employee/firm characteristics (Tables 6-7), EGC interactions (Tables 9-10), ppmlhdfe, alternative clustering, binary outcomes, and other rating dimensions, all with controls and extra FE.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Synthetic data: 59 distinct first-treated year-quarters among 783 switcher firms; 44 distinct IPO years overall including pre-sample IPOs. Real-data counts unknown.
modern_estimators_named: did_multiplegt (listed in README as required package)
csdid (listed in README as required package)
modern_estimator_note: README lists did_multiplegt and csdid among required packages and mentions 'alternative estimators' among robustness tests, but the shipped do-file (LP_SyntheticData.do) contains no such call.

specs.treatment_definition: 1 if the review is posted after the firm's IPO event date (fdate_s1, else ipodate); 0 before and for private firms
specs.cluster: cluster_var (equals firm-by-year cells in the synthetic data)

specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying controls and additional additive FE (state_code job_title_code tenure_years)
specs.notes: This FE set is used for all cross-sectional, robustness and other-outcome regressions (lines 103-177), which are therefore all ineligible.

specs.treatment_var: minus3 minus2 minus1 one two three
specs.treatment_definition: relative-year bins around the IPO built from years_since_ipo and nq (quarters since S-1/IPO): minus3 = years_since_ipo < -2, minus2 = -2, minus1 = -1, one = 1, two = 2, three = > 2; IPO year (zero) omitted; all bins 0 for never-treated reviews
specs.notes: Omitted period is relative year 0, not -1; bins adjusted by quarter counts (lines 283-292). Columns 2-3 (lines 297, 300) add controls / extra FE and are ineligible.

specs.time_var: year_qtr (FE); data collapsed to firm by year_month3
specs.data_file: FINAL_synthetic_dataset1.dta (collapsed in a preserve block, lines 186-196)
specs.reported_location: uncertain: Figure 2 (monthly analysis) or Tables 11-12 (robustness); verify against article
specs.notes: Window keeps all pre-IPO and never-treated observations plus post-IPO months within the window.

specs.exclusion_reason: subgroup-by-treatment interactions (c.post_ipo_dummy##c.at_ipo, manager, max_comp1, small, big_4, high_tenure_cut, entrenched) plus controls and extra FE

specs.fe: firm year_qtr (col 1-2); plus job_title_code i.tenure_years state_code (col 3)
specs.sample_condition: year_s1 > 2004 & post_egc_period == 0 | private_company == 1; non-EGC IPOs after 2010 and firms with revenue > $1B dropped

data_files: lp_gvkeys_final.dta (gvkeys of public firms in the final sample)
output_log_synthetic.txt (Stata log of LP_SyntheticData.do on synthetic data 1)
data_files_note: Shipped files are labelled 'SYNTHETIC DATA - Li & Pinto (2023)'. README: raw Glassdoor review data are proprietary (obtained under agreement with Glassdoor), and the authors state they cannot share actual code files, only the synthetic-data do-file. Variables in the synthetic file match the do-file. Some synthetic variables are generated at random in the do-file (entrenched, high_comp2 when missing). Only the do-file for dataset1 is shipped; the role of datasets 2 and 3 is undocumented.
software_notes: Stata 17+/18 (reghdfe, ppmlhdfe, estout, coefplot); SAS for data preparation; Python for RepRisk name matching.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Design qualifies, but the only data are synthetic, so TWFE/CSA/BJS estimates from the package would not reproduce published numbers; real data require a Glassdoor agreement. Table/column mapping of the firm-month window regressions is inferred and must be checked against the article. The README's reference to did_multiplegt/csdid robustness tests is not reflected in the shipped code.
